book.title: Between Two Worlds: Jewish War Brides after the Holocaust

argument.statement: Proponents viewed marriages between Jewish women and Allied military personnel as a means to rebuild lives and help Jewish repopulation after the Holocaust beyond merely leaving war-torn Europe.

book.summary: Facing the harrowing task of rebuilding a life in the wake of the Holocaust, many Jewish survivors, community and religious leaders, and Allied soldiers viewed marriage between Jewish women and military personnel as a way to move forward after unspeakable loss. Proponents believed that these unions were more than just a ticket out of war-torn Europe: they would help the Jewish people repopulate after the attempted annihilation of European Jewry. Historian Robin Judd, whose grandmother survived the Holocaust and married an American soldier after liberation, introduces us to the Jewish women who lived through genocide and went on to wed American, Canadian, and British military personnel after the war.
